newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa sinks at midday on spec liquidation.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa sinks at midday on spec liquidation.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures sank at midday under a wave of speculative long liquidation, dealers said.
But steady scale-down manufacturer buying, as well as light trade interest, stemmed further losses, they added.
"It's pretty much what we've been seeing the last couple of days -- spec selling into manufacturer and trade buying," said one trader.
At 1201 EDT, benchmark September was down $18 at $1,465 a tonne, traded $1,488 to $1,462. Second-month December was $17 lower at $1,512, while the back months fell $13 to $18.
Cocoa prices headed higher at the outset, as expected, in line with gains overnight in London. Traders said September's inability to get past chart resistance at $1,490 dampened buyers' enthusiasm.
They also said a still-strong dollar against sterling and other European currencies weighed on the market.
"There was a little currency-related arb selling early on, but they have backed off," said a trader.
Downward momentum accelerated after September fell through $1,475, triggering sell-stop orders.
On the charts, traders said September now faced support at $1,460, followed by $1,448 and $1,438 to $1,436. Resistance was still seen near $1,490.
Volume as of 1100 EDT was heavy, at an estimated 7,076 lots.
